challenges.title: Saudi Labor Law, Ramadan and the 12-Hour Limit

items.title: Standard Hours & the 6-Day Limit
items.text: Standard working time is capped at 8 hours per day or 48 hours per week (Art. 98). Since the 2025 reform, an additional rule applies: no more than 6 consecutive working days without a full rest day.

items.title: Ramadan: Shorter Shifts, Automatically
items.text: For Muslim staff, actual working hours mandatorily drop during شهر رمضان (Shahr Ramadan) to a maximum of 6 hours per day or 36 hours per week — recalculated every year for exactly this group.

items.title: 12-Hour Presence Limit (Art. 101)
items.text: No employee may remain at the workplace (التواجد في مكان العمل) for more than 12 hours — including breaks, prayer and meal times. In addition, after a maximum of 5 hours of continuous work, a break of at least 30 minutes is mandatory.

solutions.title: How Klacks Takes the Load Off Businesses in Saudi Arabia
solutions.subtitle: From automatic 12-hour monitoring to your own infrastructure — it all fits together.

items.title: Standard Hours & 6-Day Limit Monitored
items.text: Klacks knows the 8h/48h limit (Art. 98) and the new rule of max. 6 consecutive working days without a rest day — violations simply never occur.

items.title: Ramadan Hours Reduced Automatically
items.text: For Muslim staff, Klacks automatically schedules with the reduced 6h/36h limit (Art. 98) during Ramadan — without manually reworking the entire plan.

items.title: 12-Hour Limit Strictly Enforced (Art. 101)
items.text: Klacks blocks shift sequences that would keep a person at the workplace for more than 12 hours — including breaks, prayer and meal times.

items.title: Overtime Premium under Art. 107
items.text: The statutory premium of 50% on the base wage (effectively 150%) is calculated automatically — since the 2025 reform, optionally also as paid time off in lieu.

items.title: Nitaqat Saudization Tracked
items.text: Klacks tracks which Saudi employees with a GOSI-insured salary of SAR 4,000 or more count as a full quota unit (1.0), and which count as only 0.5 (SAR 3,000 to 3,999).

items.title: On-Premise: Data Stays in Saudi Arabia
items.text: Klacks runs on your own infrastructure, and you choose the AI model. Sensitive biometric time-tracking data (البيانات الشخصية الحساسة) stays physically within KSA — eliminating the cross-border compliance burden under PDPL/SDAIA.

items.title: Klacksy: Rule-Based, No Black Box
items.text: The built-in Klacksy AI assistant schedules by voice command — transparently, based on defined skills and rules, not as an opaque AI decision.

klacksy.title: Klacksy: The Built-In Assistant for Your Team
klacksy.text: Klacksy isn’t a bolted-on marketing chatbot — it’s embedded directly in the Klacks interface. Staff and schedulers ask about shift times via chat or check availability. A built-in skills and rules system ensures Klacksy makes transparent suggestions — never a black-box decision. For businesses with strict PDPL/SDAIA compliance requirements, the AI model can also be hosted locally in Saudi Arabia.

example.title: Ramadan Shifts and the 12-Hour Limit, at a Glance
